title: The Lotus Sutra
altTitles: The Lotus of the True Law
attributionNote: The sutra is anonymous, composed in India over several generations and expanded as it travelled through Central Asia and East Asia. It is not ascribed to a single author.
description: The Lotus Sutra is the most influential Mahayana scripture in East Asia, in twenty-seven chapters: the Buddha's declaration that all beings can attain Buddhahood, the parable of the burning house, the jewel in the robe, the story of the dragon king's daughter, the appearance of the stupa of Many Treasures, the cosmic lifespan of the Buddha, and the bodhisattva practices of the universal gate. Its teaching of the one vehicle shaped Tiantai, Tendai, Nichiren and much of Chinese and Japanese Buddhism.
historicalContext: The Saddharma-puṇḍarīka survives in Sanskrit, Tibetan and Chinese recensions; the Chinese translation of Kumārajīva (406) became the standard East Asian text. H. Kern's translation, published in the Sacred Books of the East, volume 21 (1884), is the first complete English rendering from the Sanskrit and remains a standard public-domain edition.
availabilityNote: Complete. All twenty-seven chapters of Kern's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The volume's introduction is not part of the work.
